xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:BriefDetailsOfCyberSecurityInc: Suspicious email was received by user Chowdaiah Thogata at tchowdaiah@mazdock.com and reported to CSO-MDL. The email was in a foreign language (Japanese) and does not have any attachment. The email had header as ‘Apple’ logo and something like Javascript/ Python programming language which has VAR, timestamp, random value as seen in bottom of the email content. The email had a link in Japanese language which appears suspicious. The sender was unknown to receiver. The Incident was registered & categorised as Spam Email -CERT. The Suspicious email-ID was blocked and has been deleted from the system. The above mentioned incident has been reported to CERT-In, CIRA & CSG-DDP.

Suspicious email was received by user J Kumaran at jkumaran@mazdock.com and reported to CSO-MDL. The email refers to an attachment (a pdf document) regarding Agenda Points for Joint Venture Meeting at IHQ MoD on 04 Feb 2025. The email Subject was : ‘Agenda Points for Joint Venture Meeting at IHQ MoD on 04 Feb 2025’. The attachment asks for identity confirmation and to confirm with NIC/Gov.in email account. The sender was unknown to receiver. Similar mails have been received by the user in the past also. The Incident was registered & categorised as Spam Email -CERT. The Suspicious email-ID was blocked and has been deleted from the system. The above mentioned incident has been reported to CERT-In, CIRA & CSG-DDP.

During the quarter ended 31.12.2024, the company did not comply with Regulations 17, 18, 19 and 21 of SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015 due to which the NSE and BSE imposed penalty for non-compliance of Rs. 592360 each.
On achieving compliance of Regulations 18, 19 and 21, the Company has applied for waiver of the Penalty from NSE, the designated Stock Exchange.
For Regulation 17, the power to appoint Directors is vested with the President of India acting through the Ministry of Defence, Department of Defence Production and not in the control of the Company. Company shall apply for waiver of Regulation 17 on achieving compliance.

xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: Total Disputed amount of Rs. 7563 Lakhs. The subject appeal has been filed by the Commissioner of Sales Tax against the order dated 27.04.2018 passed by the Second Bench of Maharashtra Sales Tax Tribunal in favour of MDL in respect of tax issues pertaining to medium refit cum upgradation of INS Shalki & INS Shankul. MDL's contention in respect of medium refit-cum-upgradation contract of INS Shalki & Shankul is that it is a sale in the course of import and cannot be subjected to tax. In order to avoid payment of any interest and penalty MDL has paid tax under composition @ 8% amounting to Rs. 7563 Lakhs. The Financial claim / impact in the appeal would be Rs. 7563 Lakhs The Appeal has been admitted by the Bombay High Court vide its order dated 21.02.2019. The Appeal is yet to be listed for hearing.
